Wiener's office reports SB 53 was signed on 2025-09-29: a California frontier-AI law from the same sponsor. This refutes literal abandonment, but it is the sponsor's own release, and enactment alone says nothing about any chilling effect.
The official transcript of the 2025-05-19 signing of the Take It Down Act, a federal law covering AI deepfakes. It shows federal action went on, but it is narrow and not tied to the veto.

reviews.rationale: The condition was met: the bill was vetoed. Read literally, 'nobody will bother' is refuted by SB 53 and the Take It Down Act. Nothing in the packet shows a 'Big Tech always wins' view spreading, or later efforts being weakened compared with what would otherwise have happened. The contract's contradiction condition needs both parts, and no part is supported, so the overall result is unresolved.

contract.note: Treating these as credible risks rather than realised harms, and the cause as contributing rather than the only cause, is the ordinary reading. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: NIST AI 600-1, July 2024, published before the post. It lists bias, harmful content, disinformation, privacy, IP and environmental risks, and ties estimation difficulty to diverse uses and immature science. It is labelled a secondary summary but is really a primary NIST report.
Bommasani et al. (v3, 2022): reuse across applications passes defects downstream, and understanding of how models work and fail is limited. This backs the causal mechanism.
The May 2024 international scientific interim report covers bias, labour-market disruption, privacy, environmental effects and defamatory synthetic media. It also hedges on the net effect on jobs.

reviews.rationale: Authoritative assessments published before the post document credible risks in the listed categories. They tie the spread of these risks, and the difficulty of managing them, to broad applicability and limited understanding. The packet holds no counterevidence. Employment effects are still uncertain, but the claim is about risk, not proven job loss.
